record.original_question: If n_1 < ... < n_k are positive integers that are multiplicatively dependent, must there be at least one prime in the interval [n_1, n_k]?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.8 (Langevin). Given an increasing sequence n1 < n2 < · · · < nk of positive integers such that n1 , n2 , . . . , nk are multiplicatively dependent, there exists a prime number in the interval [n1 , nk ].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a finite set of positive integers $\{n_1, n_2, \dots, n_k\}$ (with $k \ge 2$) multiplicatively dependent if there exist integers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$, not all zero, such that
$$n_1^{a_1} n_2^{a_2} \cdots n_k^{a_k} = 1.$$
Prove or disprove: for every increasing sequence $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots < n_k$ of positive integers that is multiplicatively dependent, the closed interval $[n_1, n_k]$ contains at least one prime number.
artifact.category_tag: primes in intervals and multiplicative dependence
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return authoritative sources confirming a resolution of Langevin's conjecture on the existence of a prime in the interval determined by a multiplicatively dependent sequence of positive integers. No paper claiming a proof or disproof was located, so the status appears to be open but could not be definitively verified.
